world.bio: Mateus Ferraz, 28, São Paulo. Paint murals in Vila Madalena, mostly in the Beco do Batman and around the Vila Madalena metro, sell prints and stickers at the weekend fair at Praça Benedito Calixto. Grew up in Capão Redondo, learned on walls near my mum's house. Style is big birds in flat colour, a little bit of graphic and a lot of grain. Play drums in a band called Quintal that rehearses on Thursdays.
skills_assets: Mural painter, forty-plus walls across the city since 2019, from three-storey buildings to garage doors
Sells prints and stickers at the Benedito Calixto weekend fair, around R$3,000 a month on a good month
Instagram with 14k followers, mostly local and Latin American
Owns scaffolding access, a ladder truck rental contact, and a set of Montana and Molotow cans
Prints on Hahnemühle paper through a local print shop, editions of 50
Plays drums, rehearses Thursdays in a garage in Pinheiros

projects.name: Wall at Rua Wisard
projects.text: Eight metres by five, a heron over a flooded street. Owner of the building commissioned it, 6,000 reais plus paint. Half done. Weather keeps interrupting. Finishing by the 20th, hopefully.

projects.name: Print edition: Garças
projects.text: Series of six bird prints, edition of 50 each. Got them back from the printer, signing and numbering this week. Selling for R$180 each at the fair, R$280 framed.

projects.name: The T-shirt thing
projects.text: A clothing brand put one of his wall pieces on a T-shirt without asking and he only found out from a friend's Instagram story. Brand is a mid-sized São Paulo streetwear label, sells the shirt for R$149. The piece is a blue macaw on a building in Vila Madalena I painted in 2022. They didn't credit me. Their post has 3k likes. I don't know what to do about it.

notes.text: Neighbour complained again about the smell of spray. Dona Luzia, who has lived in the building next to the studio for forty years. I apologised, brought her a bag of pão de queijo, she softened. She said, 'Your birds are lovely but my lungs are not.' Fair.

Rehearsal Thursday: Quintal played the whole new set. Bruno on bass dropped a beat in the bridge and we laughed for ten minutes. Something about playing drums after painting all day, my arms feel like they belong to someone else.

Friend Camila texted me a screenshot of a T-shirt on the Instagram story of a streetwear brand called Concreto. My macaw. My blue macaw from Rua Aspicuelta. On a shirt. Not credited. Not asked. A hundred and forty-nine reais. I stared at it for a long time. First feeling was pride, which I'm ashamed of. Second feeling was something else.
Searched the brand's other products. They have six prints from different street artists, none credited. Left a comment under the post, 'Nice, who's the artist?' It was deleted in ten minutes.

Talked to my friend who is a law student. She said copyright applies to murals in Brazil but the building owner's rights, the public location, all complicate it. She suggested a formal notification letter first. Said I should document everything. Screenshots, dates, the original photos of my wall. I have those.

My grandmother in Minas Gerais had a fall. Mum drove up this weekend. She's okay, but frail. She keeps saying she doesn't need help. Mum said she hasn't eaten properly for days. Sold two prints at the fair and wired mum a bit of money for the trip.

Went to the wall at Rua Wisard. Rain forecast. Covered the unfinished part with plastic and tape. Sat on a bucket and drank coffee. The heron's neck is the best thing I've done in months. Don't want to lose it to the weather.

Wrote a draft email to the clothing brand. Four versions. One angry, one polite, one that offered to collaborate, one that threatened legal action. Sent none. Don't want to burn a door I might need, and also don't want to be someone who lets it go.

Fair day. A woman asked if I was the guy who did the blue macaw on Aspicuelta. I said yes. She said she saw it on a shirt and thought it was a collab. I said no. She frowned. She bought two prints and said she'd stop buying from them. Small win.

Finished signing and numbering the Garças series. Kept the artist proofs. Rain on the mural, again. Mum called from Minas. Grandma is better. I told her about the shirt. She said, 'Meu filho, you did the work, you decide.'

messages.text:
Camila: Is this your macaw??
Me: Where did you see this?
Camila: Concreto brand story.
Me: Send me the link.

Bruno: Thursday still on?
Me: Yes.
Bruno: Bring the new sticks.
Me: I broke them all.

Mum: I'm at the hospital with vovó.
Me: Is she okay?
Mum: She's stable.
Me: Call me tonight.

Friend: Draft notice, take a look.
Me: Looks strong.
Friend: Don't send until we've checked their trademarks.
Me: Okay.

Print shop: Edition ready for pick-up.
Me: Great, tomorrow morning.
Print shop: Bring cash.
Me: Always.

calendar.event: Finish wall at Rua Wisard (weather permitting)

relations.about: Works as a school cook, supports my art in private, worries in public
My grandmother, 81, lives alone in a small town in Minas Gerais
Close friend, photographer, spots things on Instagram before I do
Neighbour, complains, but also waters my plants

constraints: Won't paint over other artists' walls
Won't take corporate commissions that need a fixed message
No weekend work on Saturday fair days
Won't pursue legal action that costs more than a month's income
sensitive: Anger about the shirt, mixed with fear of looking petty
